knowledge: Three consumers once each hand-wrote the same lane driver, so the minimal example shows how little a lane must supply once the shared driver and config exist. Examples read everything from the environment with placeholders. Demos that need a live backend or a terminal can only be scored on import, refusal to start and stub behaviour.
measures_of_success: Each example compiles, imports, reaches its help or not-configured exit in a scrubbed environment, appears in the index, and passes the secret and path scan. Standing conditions: Keep every example runnable on an empty environment. Keep each introduced in the index. Keep secrets and machine paths out.
parameters: Each example takes its own command-line modes (check, once, loop) and reads configuration from a file layered under environment variables, with the environment winning.
inputs: A config file and environment variables; no secrets are baked in.
outputs: A running lane or a built runner configuration, and help or not-configured messages on an empty environment.
effects: The lane example may poll a backend when configured; offline paths have none.
usage_notes: Copy the minimal lane to start, adapt the custom consumer for a specific organisation, and add a file to the index in the same change.

name: Queued-task runner lane
description: A queued task runs once, under the persona it names, and always comes back with a reported result, including after a restart.
purpose: Takes a person's queued requests to a reported outcome, so they run on time without anyone having to start them by hand.
approach: Claims each due task once, runs it, and reports the result back to its queue.
out_of_scope: Deciding what a queued task should say or do.
milestones: 1. Every lifecycle case passes on the lane's poller and executor: done, failed, needs-you, duplicate, lost claim, not-yet-due, team-scoped and unconfigured. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Discovery is event driven with signature dedup across restarts and a backend-aware claim as a second guard. A persona activates only when asked for, never from a bare mention of a name. Folder sync keeps human text and pushes each bullet once. Cancelled tasks need no patch because the backend already set the status.
measures_of_success: Poll, claim, run and report behave correctly across done, failed, needs-you, duplicate, lost-claim, not-yet-due, team-scoped and unconfigured cases, with persona choice, folder sync and scheduling correct. Standing conditions: Claim each due task once. Run it as the right persona against its work folder. Report an outcome for every task. Run none early.
parameters: The poller takes a configuration with credentials, team, adapters and a concurrency bound; personas take a skills root, registry, assignment fields and flags for model-judged asks; the lane driver takes check, once or loop modes and an env file.
inputs: Queued tasks from the backend, the configuration, persona registry and folder map.
outputs: A reported status on each task (with result text or decision id), updated folder sync files, and logs.
effects: Claims tasks on the backend, writes the sync file in work folders, may post notes, and spawns deep runs.
usage_notes: Start a lane with the shared driver and pick one-shot mode for cron or loop mode for a service. Use structured assignment for personas where tasks name an owner.

name: Layered lane configuration loader
description: Combines a lane's configuration file and environment variables into one checked configuration at startup, refusing unknown keys before the lane runs and falling back to defaults when a tuning value is bad.
purpose: Gives whoever runs a lane one predictable configuration, built from its file and its environment in a fixed order.
approach: Merges a configuration file and environment variables into one validated runner configuration, by a fixed order of precedence.
out_of_scope: Connecting the adapters a configuration names, and changing any setting for one request or turn.
milestones: 1. Every precedence rule holds in every probed combination, every invalid key is refused before the lane starts, and a bad tuning value falls back to its default: all 36 offline cases pass. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: A lane is operated by people who edit a file and export variables, so a silent typo or a surprising winner between sources costs a deployment. Past design lessons: the file is a baseline, the core package must never read the process environment directly, and tuning values must tolerate bad input by falling back to defaults so a running process can be retuned without a restart.
measures_of_success: Every precedence rule holds in every probed combination, every invalid key is refused loudly before the lane starts, and a bad tuning value never stops the lane.
parameters: A path to a TOML file (or none), plus the set of file-expressible fields owned by the configuration dataclass; tuning values are read from an optional environment mapping.
inputs: The configuration file text, additional environment files it references, the process environment, and the environment tables inside the file.
outputs: A populated runner configuration object, or a configuration-file error naming the offending key; tuning values come back as one typed settings value.
effects: Exports file-defined environment values into the process environment where the precedence rules allow, and installs the tuning-settings provider used by the core package.
usage_notes: Call at startup, before building any adapter; use the file for baselines and environment variables for per-deployment overrides. Add a file-expressible field only together with its precedence or validation rule.

name: Non-interactive command-line surface
description: Gives people and a deep run's shell one fixed command-line contract for the runner and its tool catalog, with exit codes that scripts can rely on.
purpose: Let a person or an agent's shell run the runner's tools from the command line with predictable parsing, output and exit codes.
approach: Route every command-line request through named subcommands with a fixed usage, output and exit-code contract.
out_of_scope: Running an interactive chat session, a polling loop, or a server for channels or files, which need a live terminal or server.
milestones: 1. Every subcommand answers help, malformed or unknown input is refused with the usage code, write methods are refused without the write flag, and the tool catalog lists, shows and calls tools correctly, on the offline cases. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: A deep run reaches the same tools through a shell, so the command line is a fixed contract that other processes depend on. Design lessons: write-capable methods must be refused unless explicitly allowed, maintenance commands default to a dry run, and missing credentials must produce a message that says what to set.
measures_of_success: Every subcommand answers help, unknown commands and flags and malformed arguments are refused with the usage code, write methods are refused without the write flag, and the tool catalog lists, shows and calls tools correctly.
parameters: A subcommand with its flags; the quest command takes a method name and keyword pairs, the context commands take store locations and an apply flag, the tool entry point takes list, show or call with keyword or JSON arguments.
inputs: The argument vector, the process environment for credentials, and files or a store folder the command points at.
outputs: Text on standard output and error and an integer exit code, with zero for success and the usage code for a refused invocation.
effects: Write subcommands change Quest data or card stores only when explicitly allowed; context maintenance commands are dry runs unless an apply flag is given.
usage_notes: Use from scripts and from a deep run's shell; prefer the read-only form first, add the write or apply flag deliberately, and add a case when a subcommand or flag is added.

name: Cost-ordered model tier selector with outage and allowance recovery
description: Starts each piece of work on the cheapest rung its difficulty allows and tracks new releases by family name, so the choice improves when a new model ships without an edit.
purpose: Choose the model rung that starts each piece of work, and resume work after a provider outage or usage limit rather than failing it.
approach: Start each piece of work on the rung its difficulty calls for, and step down a tier when that tier is exhausted.
out_of_scope: Judging whether the cheapest model still succeeded, which needs live runs.
milestones: 1. Tier-selection cases passed by the live rule: 42 of 42, with a pin always winning and an exhausted tier falling to the next cheaper one. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: The planner already rates difficulty on the call that decides the route, so starting-model choice costs no extra model call. Past incidents: queued tasks failed outright when a provider briefly overloaded and had to be rerun by hand, and a subscription allowance limit looks like a failed run rather than an outage, so each needs its own recognition and a resume time.
measures_of_success: Each difficulty maps to the stated starting rung, family names track new releases without edits, a pin always wins, an exhausted tier falls to the next cheaper one, and outages and limits are recognised with a correct resume time.
parameters: A difficulty rating, a ladder of rungs, optional operator model mapping and pins, a tier or family name, the list of live models, and the current time for limit parsing.
inputs: The planner's difficulty rating, a provider's live model list, error or result text from a failed model call, and the clock.
outputs: A starting model and ladder, a concrete model id for a tier or family, the next lower tier, a vision-capability answer, an outage verdict, and a usage-limit record with its reset and resume times.
effects: Remembers the latest outage and usage limit lane-wide, optionally persisted to a file, so other tasks hold off until the resume time.
usage_notes: Resolve names through the registry at the point of use rather than pinning release ids; set an operator pin only when a specific model is required. Treat an outage as a reason to requeue, not to fail the task.

name: Cost estimation, daily budget and host load guard
description: Stops a lane's spending at a daily token budget and pauses task pickup under host overload, without ever killing work already running.
purpose: Keeps a lane's spending and host load predictable, so a runaway day cannot drain the budget or overload the machine.
approach: Estimates what each operation will cost and holds back new work once a daily budget or host limit is reached.
out_of_scope: Real provider invoices, output-token billing, and work run on a subscription-based runner, which the daily budget does not count.
milestones: 1. Prices, cost estimates, the daily total across restarts, and the pause-and-resume guard for memory, free memory and load pass every offline case. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Shallow orchestrator calls can run away on cost, so a daily cap is opt-in and persisted. Pausing pickup is lossless because unclaimed tasks stay queued and fire on a later scan. Prices are a hand-kept snapshot of list prices, so a provider change is not noticed until the table is edited.
measures_of_success: Prices and estimates are arithmetically right, the daily total survives a restart and resets each day, bad or negative values are handled, and the guard pauses and resumes without flapping.
parameters: Provider and model names, a token count, daily limit and usage path from the environment, and optional host limits for memory percent, free memory and load.
inputs: Token counts per call, environment variables, and host samples of memory and load.
outputs: A price per million input tokens, a bootstrap cost estimate with the provider and model used, a running total with an over-limit flag and status line, and a paused or not verdict.
effects: Writes the day's tally to a usage file and signals the poller to stop picking up new tasks while over budget or overloaded; in-flight tasks are never killed.
usage_notes: Both limits are opt-in; set them per lane. Review the price table whenever a provider changes prices.

description: Finds broken imports, unresolved fixtures and parametrisation errors in every test file at collection time, before any test runs.
purpose: Keeps the test suite trustworthy as it grows, so a test that cannot start is found before a full run.
approach: Collects each test file on its own and reports any that fail to import, parametrise or resolve their fixtures.
out_of_scope: Whether the tests pass, or whether they stay offline, which a test run decides.
milestones: 1. Every test file collects with its imports, parametrisations and fixtures resolved: all 29 collection cases pass. [met: 2026-10-22]

name: Public-repository hygiene scanner
description: Checks the working files of a public repository for secrets, machine paths and real identifiers before they are committed, and lets documented placeholders pass.
purpose: Help a team publish a codebase in public without leaking keys, machine paths, real identifiers or addresses.
approach: Scan working files for secret shapes and consumer-specific values, and fail the run when any are found.
out_of_scope: Reviewing git history for secrets that were committed earlier.
milestones: 1. Every planted secret kind is found, every documented placeholder stays quiet, and the repository scans clean with the command exiting with failure on any finding. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: A public repository must hold nothing consumer specific or secret, and documentation needs to show the shape of a secret without being flagged, so placeholders are explicitly allowed. A secret already committed must be rotated, since the scan does not read history. Findings print a redacted snippet, never the whole secret.
measures_of_success: Every planted secret kind is found, every documented placeholder stays quiet, the repository scans clean, and the command exits with failure on any finding.
parameters: A repository root, an option to scan only staged files, and optional file selection.
inputs: Text or files known to git (tracked, or untracked and not ignored).
outputs: A list of findings with a pattern name, a location and a redacted snippet, and an exit code that is nonzero on any finding.
effects: None; it reads files only and changes nothing.
usage_notes: Run before every commit, including staged-only mode in a commit step. Add a pattern and a planted test case together whenever a new credential shape appears.

description: Turns a solution's name into the implementation the code declares, so the selected implementation can change in configuration without touching any caller.
purpose: Choose which declared implementation of each solution runs, from a configured name or the project default, so an operator can change it without a code change.
approach: Resolve each solution to its declared implementation by name, falling back to the project default when no name is set.
milestones: 1. Selection cases passed by the live resolver: 36 of 36, with a typo in a selection entry degrading to no deep runner instead of raising.

name: Documentation coverage and voice check
description: Keeps the runner's documents complete against the code: every variable, subcommand and public name has a described entry, and every relative link resolves.
purpose: Lets a newcomer or an AI learn the runner from its documents, with checks that keep them complete and in the house voice.
approach: Checks each document against the code it describes, so gaps in coverage, broken links and voice faults fail loudly.
out_of_scope: Judging whether the prose is clear or correct, and checking examples by running them.
milestones: 1. Documentation coverage and voice conformance: no document fails the em dash cases when re-recorded. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Documentation drifts unless coverage is generated from the repository: cases are produced from the code and a coverage case fails when a document or variable has no case. The house voice forbids em dashes, and a mechanical replacement changes meaning, so each is rewritten by hand.
measures_of_success: Every generated documentation case passes: no broken link, no document unreachable from the index, nothing undocumented, no em dash.
parameters: The documents folder, an index file, a generated configuration reference, and the generator that produces cases.
inputs: The markdown files, the package's public names and the real argument tree.
outputs: Pass or fail per case, naming the broken link, missing description or offending document.
effects: None; documents are read only.
usage_notes: Update the index when adding a document, document each new variable and subcommand, and regenerate cases rather than hand-editing them.

name: Scoped prediction store
description: Keeps each scope's learned patterns, live predictions and outcome log across turns and restarts, through a store that never raises into a turn, so a failed write costs that write and never a reply.
purpose: Remembers, for each scope, what an anticipation engine has learned, across turns and restarts.
approach: Saves each scope's patterns, predictions and outcome log, and returns them only to the scope they belong to.
out_of_scope: Judging whether a prediction was right, and sharing learned patterns across scopes.
milestones: 1. A store passes every persistence contract scenario (round trip, isolation, replace, expiry, view, clear, log, restart and tolerance) with no store call raising: all 12 cases pass on the file store. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: The store sits behind a port so a consumer with its own database can supply one. Storage must be best-effort and never raise into a turn. Prediction quality is a separate unmeasured question: the engine logs each prediction against the actual next message, but no replayed corpus scores it.
measures_of_success: A store passes every contract scenario: round trip, isolation, replace, expiry, view, clear, log, restart and tolerance.
parameters: A scope key per call, patterns, predictions with an expiry time and optional views, and a log record.
inputs: Pattern and prediction records and the scope key.
outputs: The saved patterns, the unexpired predictions, a precomputed view text by prediction id, or nothing for a write.
effects: Writes persistent state (a file per scope and an outcome log in the file store) and drops expired predictions on load.
usage_notes: Implement the port's methods to add a backend and run the same contract scenarios against it; choose the file store for a lane, an in-memory store only as a reference.

name: Autopilot run-or-skip gate
description: Judges cadence in the quest's own time zone and by a roster of days, so a background pass runs when the person's settings allow and waits otherwise, while a Run now request or a reactive trigger can override the cadence.
purpose: Keep background AI work to the days, hours and budget a person has set, so no quest is worked on or charged when the person did not allow it.
approach: Check each quest's own settings (budget, cadence, roster, holds) before a pass reads any goal or calls a model.
out_of_scope: Choosing what a pass works on once it has been allowed to run.
milestones: 1. Every labelled gate case ends as skipped for the right reason or as past every gate, on both the development and the held-out shares. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: A wrong run spends and sends against the person's setting, and a wrong skip loses a day, so the gate is a rule, not a quality dial. Cadence is judged in the quest's own time zone with a roster of days, not by elapsed time, and a pending Run now request or a reactive trigger can override cadence. Backpressure also holds a quest.
measures_of_success: Every labelled gate case ends as skipped for the right reason or as past every gate, and a baseline that uses elapsed-time cadence with no roster fails the cases.
parameters: A daily budget, a backpressure flag, a clock, and per-quest autopilot settings (cadence, Run now, reactive trigger, roster days).
inputs: The quest list, each quest's autopilot settings, open tasks and asks, open decisions, and the current time.
outputs: For each quest, either a skip with a reason or passage through every gate to the work stage.
effects: Counts against the daily budget when a quest is worked; before the gates pass, no goals are read and no model is called.
usage_notes: Place every eligibility rule in the gate, before any expensive read, and add a case for each new rule or setting.

name: Evolve by metric
description: Keeps every part of QAR comparable by its metric, so a better model, method or tool replaces the current one by measurement instead of by rewrite.
purpose: Keep every part of QAR specified as a solution with alternatives, a metric and a selected implementation, so the best one is used as the state of the art moves.
approach: Select each part's implementation by its recorded measurement, and replace it when a rival measures better on the same cases.
out_of_scope: It avoids saying what QAR is for: that is the top intent, and the general machinery for checking, measuring and selecting is the evolvable-structure library's.
milestones: 1. Share of QAR solutions whose selected implementation has a recorded result on committed code and is not beaten by a rival on the same cases: 100%.
knowledge: The author's evolvable structure (intents, problems, solutions, implementations, ideals and metrics); the evolvable-structure library's checks, measurement harness and selector.
measures_of_success: Every solution has a recorded result on committed code, selections follow the measurements, and Joshua can steer by reviewing metrics without reading code. Standing conditions: Every part of QAR has a record, a current measured result and a selection that follows the measurement; a better model, method or tool replaces the current one without a rewrite.
parameters: The records under esoi, the esoi configuration, the evaluation components.
inputs: A change to the code, a new alternative, or a new model or tool to compare.
outputs: Checked records, recorded metric results and the selected implementation for each solution.
effects: Result rows are appended to the evaluation log; no model spend unless a paid arm is run by decision.
usage_notes: Run esoi check before committing and esoi run --stale after committing measured code. Paid arms follow the metric run policy.

name: Intent frame for quest-scoped prompts
description: Puts a quest's purpose into every prompt about it as a small slice built from stored records, at no model cost and within a fixed size limit.
purpose: Keeps a person's quest work tied to its purpose by showing the intent each quest serves to whatever answers it.
approach: Builds a short frame from a quest's intent, ideals, metrics and gaps, and passes it to the prompt with a pointer to drill in.
out_of_scope: Whole specifications pasted into a prompt, and quests with no intent behind them, which get nothing added.
milestones: 1. The intent-grounded pass rate is recorded for each arm of the single-call ladder, with the frame arm compared against the arm without it.
knowledge: The backend builds the frame (app/business/intents/frame.py) and serves it at the intents frame endpoint; the autopilot brief, the chat quest facts and the quest card carry it. Gaps are queries over ids, never model judgments.
measures_of_success: A larger share of cases whose right answer depends on the intent are answered correctly with the frame than without, at small extra input cost, and cases with no intent are unchanged. Standing conditions: Keep the slice under a fixed small token ceiling. Add nothing for an unsorted quest or a person with no intents.
parameters: The slice carries a fixed token ceiling and names the card of the intent so the model can drill in; the carrier is chosen per surface.
inputs: A quest id and the viewer.
outputs: Frame text, an anchor (intent, solution, implementation, quest ids) and what sits directly below it.
effects: Read-only database queries on the backend; no model call; the autopilot brief grows by the frame only when the quest is placed.
usage_notes: Selection stays on the no-frame arm until the intent-grounded metric has been run by decision; the paid ladder is staged under esoi/metric-run-policy.md.

name: Specification slice before a task and write-back after
description: Starts a task from the slice of the specification it serves, and writes the run's outcome, metric movement and any record it fixed back onto those records, so the next run starts from a truer specification.
purpose: Keeps each run tied to the purpose it serves, and leaves every record it touched more accurate than it was.
approach: Reads the slice of the specification a task serves before it starts, and writes what the run changed back onto those records.
out_of_scope: A new document or file for each run or session, judging whether a change was good (the metric does that), and rewriting an owner's own vision or ideals, which change only as a proposal.
milestones: 1. Every deep run on a solution with an offline arm leaves a durable before and after reading on that solution. 2. Every run that touched a record leaves its outcome and movement on that record. 3. Every run that found a record wrong or missing fixes it in the same change, with what changed and why on the record. 4. More replayed tasks are accepted on the first attempt, with less exploration before the first edit on a repeat task.
knowledge: Repositories already carry records with a gap and an action per solution; the standing deep-run instructions carry the generic method. Already true: record_metric_result and GoalMetrics give a deep run a recorded or measured before and after per metric (core/tools_metric_results.py, core/goal_metrics.py, core/metric_meter.py); the runner reads the metric before and after the work for slice-and-writeback (core/goal_iteration.py); the executor puts metrics and metric_missing on the task report (runner/executor_reporting.py); FileContextStore.record bumps a card's usage_count, sets last_outcome from the kind of turn and stamps provenance (adapters/context_store_cards.py). Missing: the per-run file of readings sits in a temporary folder; no field says what moved; readings never reach the record; the card updater gets no metric facts; nothing makes a run fix a record it found wrong. One home per kind already exists: the results log (evaluation/components/results.csv) for metric readings; for an ESOI record, git history for the change itself plus the tracking columns of the record's row in esoi/tracker/ (the review files esoi tracker build writes, one row per record); a card's own usage fields and provenance for a card. The specification owner's direction: the AI handles specification changes itself in most cases, and changes the owner's own words only as a proposal. This solution absorbed the former track-runs-on-records on 2026-10-22, which specified the same write-back for the same runs and records.
measures_of_success: More tasks accepted on the first attempt and fewer reads before the first edit on the second task for the same solution; runs on measured solutions leave durable, attributed readings and say what moved; a record found wrong or missing is fixed in the same change with what changed and why on the record. Standing conditions: Create no new file outside the records and the code, and no file per run. The AI edits the records itself; change the owner's own words (an intent's vision statement, the ideals the owner wrote) only as a proposal. Ask a person only for the escalation triggers: information only a person has, an irreversible act, a big change of direction.
parameters: The slice size per solution; whether write-back is done by the worker in the same change; which records a run updates (the ones it was shown and used); whether a reading is recorded or measured; which fields are the owner's own words; and where a proposal or an escalation is delivered (the escalation sink).
inputs: A task, its quest or its working folder; after the run, its metric results (metric, solution, milestone, before, after), what it changed, the records it was shown and used, and any record it found wrong or missing.
outputs: A slice for the brief; per record served: the last run that touched it, its outcome, the metric movement, what moved, and the last change made to it with its reason; a proposal only for the owner's own words; an escalation only for the escalation triggers.
effects: Edits record fields directly in the same commit as the work, with the reason in the commit message and on the record's tracking columns; writes a card's usage fields and provenance; appends readings to the results log. Raises a decision request only for an escalation trigger or a proposed change to the owner's own words. No model call of its own.
usage_notes: Selected today: slice-and-writeback, whose write-back reaches a per-run file of readings and the task report only. writeback-on-the-record is the planned next implementation that carries the readings and the fixes onto the records. A person reviews by reading git history and the tracking columns, not by approving each change.

name: Core ML tasks: quest classification and recommendation
description: Puts the Quest classification and recommendation tasks under one measured choice, so each method is picked by held-out accuracy and cost rather than by habit.
purpose: Help every Quest feature that classifies a quest or input, or recommends a next goal, step or quest, use the most accurate method its measurements support.
approach: Choose the classification or recommendation method for each Quest task by its measured accuracy on held-out cases, with cost as the tie-break.
out_of_scope: Routing a single chat message to an answer, a tool or a deep run.
milestones: 1. Accuracy on held-out labelled cases is recorded for shared-quest-ranker and hybrid-candidate-ranker, then for the area-of-life and recommendation alternatives.
knowledge: Requested by Joshua on 2026-10-19: quest classification and recommendation are the main ML tasks used across Quest and have had alternative implementations. Located in code on 2026-10-19: which-quest classification in quest-backend quest_selection.py (the shared ranker) and quest_candidates.py (the chat's hybrid ranker); area-of-life classification in categories/search.py and planets_service.py; quest-to-intent placement and intent recommendation in intents/suggest.py; next-period goal placement in period_review_ai.py; message routing in evaluation/components/classification.
measures_of_success: Each task has a labelled case set with a held-out share, and every alternative has a recorded result on it; the selected alternative is the best by accuracy with cost as tie-break.
parameters: The task (classify or recommend), the implementation, and the model tier where one is used.
inputs: The quest, input text or user data to classify, or the person's quests, goals and history to recommend from.
outputs: A class or a ranked list with a score for each, and the cost of producing it.
effects: May spend model tokens; reads user data; writes nothing.
usage_notes: Define a case set per task first, then register each existing alternative as an implementation of this solution.

name: Select the intent specifications an input concerns
description: Returns the few intent records that bear on a request, found by both its words and its meaning, so no unrelated record crowds the context.
purpose: Choose, from an ESOI specification index, the few records a new request concerns and their linked records, so the work starts from the intent that applies.
approach: Select the records an input concerns from a specification index, and return none when no record concerns it.
out_of_scope: Building the specification index, and reading the chosen records in full.
milestones: 1. Labelled requests passed by the gated lexical and vector arm: 76 of 76, with every expected record present and no more than the ceiling returned.
knowledge: The ESOI specification index (version 1 JSON: entries, weighted terms, document frequencies); TF-IDF and reciprocal rank fusion; parallel batched LLM selection as in the card filter.
measures_of_success: On labelled inputs every expected record is selected; a failed vector or model call never removes a candidate; calls equal batches. Standing conditions: The records an input concerns are selected from the whole tree in one model call's latency, with no invented ids and no loss when a call fails.
parameters: k_lexical, k_vector, batch_size, max_workers, expand, model.
inputs: The request text, the loaded index, an optional model provider, an optional vector search callable returning entry ids.
outputs: A SpecSelection: ids best first then linked ids, the candidates shown to the model, which source proposed each, the number of calls and failed batches.
effects: One cheap model call per batch of candidates; none without a provider.
usage_notes: Load the index with load_spec_index (write it with `esoi spec index --out FILE`; its digest says when it is stale), pass the run's provider and the consumer's own vector search over the same entries, then read in full only the returned ids.

name: Card store growth prevention
description: Stops a card store from compounding: a copy never restates a card the store already holds, and the owner's card limit is enforced loudly, never by silent deletion.
purpose: Keeps a card store proportionate to its sources while it is built and refreshed, so a lane's memory stays a useful size.
approach: Gives each copied card an origin-based id, refuses writes that would compound or exceed the limit, and says so in a notice.
out_of_scope: Deciding which folders a corpus may read, repairing a store that has already grown, and touching a card that another system manages or a person wrote.
milestones: 1. Every card store growth case passes as the runner ships: repeated passes over nested stores add no copy of a copy, and a store at its limit refuses new derived cards with a notice. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. On every card growth case, the store opened as the runner opens it keeps cards per topic at 1.0 and duplicate share at 0, with no topic lost. [met: 2026-10-22] 3. The broken baseline (drop_every_import) and the no_cleanup arm fail the cases the selected implementation passes. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: The copy-import id rule (a namespace of the source root, two dashes, the card id, cut to 200 characters) with copies of copies kept is what compounded (docs/context-card-stores.md, containment audit defects 1 and 2). Two real stores reached 8,557 and 32,070 cards on 2026-10-05 before any guard existed. Mount mode stops copying for the stores that adopt it. The guards committed on 2026-10-22 (origin ids, a store never its own import source, the write-time id refusal, the one-root refusal, the card limit) are on in the runner. The card limit (adapters/card_limit.py) counts the store's own cards on every repository. It never trims by itself: a store found above it is left as it is and told. On a local folder a new learned or quest card at the limit moves the coldest derived card into _quarantine/limit; on the Quest backend and Qdrant, which cannot set a card aside without deleting shared data, a learned card is admitted over the limit (it cannot be rebuilt from the files) while a new bootstrap card is refused, and the notice says so. Repairing a store that already grew is a different job with a different definition of best, so it is its own solution, repair-a-card-store; both run in the runner side by side.
measures_of_success: Every card_store_growth case passes and every card_growth case keeps one card per distinct topic of its source files for the store opened as the runner opens it, with no topic lost and nothing a person or a run wrote lost. Standing conditions: prevention refuses or does not keep a card; it never deletes one. The card limit is the owner's number and is never silent: it never deletes a card, never trims a store it finds above the limit, and says what fills the store and how to change the limit.
parameters: QAR_MAX_CARDS, the most cards one store owns on any repository, 1000 by default; 0 or unlimited removes the limit. QAR_CARD_MOUNT (copy or mount mode). The folder review and risk gate decide what may be read (choose-what-to-index).
inputs: A corpus tree, the lane's card store, and the stores its bootstrap and refresh would import or mount.
outputs: Cards written only under an id made of their origin; a refused write logged as an error naming the id; the card limit's notice naming what fills the store and how to change the limit.
effects: Refuses writes that would compound or exceed the limit. At the limit on a local folder a learned or quest card moves the coldest derived card into _quarantine/limit (undone by moving the file back); on the Quest backend and Qdrant nothing is removed. The notice goes to the log, the startup callback and the next task's progress feed.
usage_notes: A lane in copy mode should move to mount mode (docs/context-card-stores.md, Migrating a deployment) so the cause stops. To change the limit set QAR_MAX_CARDS where the lane reads its environment (docs/context-card-stores.md, The card limit). A store that already inflated is repaired by repair-a-card-store, not by raising or lowering the limit.

name: Card store repair
description: Brings a card store that has grown too large back to one card per distinct topic in its source files, removing only copies it can prove and joining what they held onto the card that keeps it.
purpose: Returns an inflated card store to a size that matches its sources, so searches stay focused and nothing a person or a run wrote is lost.
approach: Plans and applies a tidy of duplicate and surplus cards through one repository interface, keeping a way to undo each change.
out_of_scope: Stopping new copies from being made, choosing which folders a corpus may read, choosing which cards suit a task, removing a card a person wrote or taught or one another system manages, and removing shared data from a hosted store without its owner's opt-in.
milestones: 1. Cards per topic is 1.0 with no duplicates and no topic lost, and nothing a person or a run wrote is lost, on every card_growth case, for the repository tidy on a backend-shaped store. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The same holds for the local folder tidy at open and for the quarantine script. 3. Every removal on a hosted store is undone by its manifest in a test against the real hosted API, not only the in-memory fake.
knowledge: Two real stores reached 8,557 and 32,070 cards on 2026-10-05 and were cleaned by moving cards into _quarantine (scripts/quarantine_cards.py). A compounded copy can be the only copy left, so it is removed only when a surviving card with the same files stays. A store on the Quest backend had no tidy at all: one lane's backend store held 5,488 cards, most of them copy-import ids, cards about excluded nested repositories and same-file duplicates. The repository tidy (adapters/card_store_tidy.py, commits 0d641cb, eab09b4 and d00777b) plans and applies the script's rules through the CardRepository port. A backend has no quarantine folder, so there it deletes, after a full local export that the manifest's undo restores from. The tidy at open of a local folder (self_heal, adapters/card_store_hygiene.py) is on in the runner's builders since commit 1503d38.
measures_of_success: Every card_growth case keeps one card per distinct topic of its source files, loses no topic, keeps the cards a person wrote or taught, the managed card and the notes a run added, and keeps two distinct topics on one file apart. Standing conditions: on a local folder a card is moved into _quarantine, never deleted; on a backend a card is deleted only after a complete export of it is written, only when the owner set card_tidy = apply or ran cards tidy --apply, and every deletion is undone by cards tidy --undo with the run's manifest. Never remove a card a person wrote or taught or another system manages, except a provable compounded copy whose holdings join its keeper. The plan is always said where the lane's owner sees it, with the command.
parameters: RunnerConfig.card_tidy (qar.toml): apply, plan or off; unset applies on a local folder and plans on the Quest backend and Qdrant. cards tidy: --config or --cards-dir, --apply, --merge-topics, --undo with a manifest. The quarantine script: the reasons to apply, the file-set overlap at which two cards count as one, excluded and kept folder prefixes, other stores that cover this one, and dry run or apply. self_heal on a local folder store (on in the runner's builders). QAR_MAX_CARDS decides when the startup tidy is due.
inputs: A card store on any repository, its folder review, and optionally other stores to compare it with.
outputs: A plan (tidy-state/last-plan.json for the startup tidy), a manifest naming every card removed or that would be removed, with its reason and the card that keeps its knowledge, a full export of every card touched, and a sentence on the log, the startup callback and the next task's progress feed.
effects: On a local folder moves card files under the store's _quarantine folder by reason; the store ignores that folder, so the index shrinks and a move is undone by moving the file back. On the Quest backend and Qdrant deletes the cards, after writing their export under the lane's own card folder (tidy-state, mode 600); cards tidy --undo re-creates them from it. Keepers gain the keywords of the cards joined onto them. Moving a card does not remove its vector point.
usage_notes: On a backend read the plan the lane announces (or run cards tidy without --apply), then apply it with the command it gives, or set card_tidy = apply to let the lane do it at startup. Keep the export and manifest: they are the only way back on a backend, and they sit on the lane's disk, so copy them elsewhere before anything happens to that disk. Repair does not stop the next growth; bound-card-growth does.

name: Unified card and specification search
description: Lets one search return a run's context cards and its specification records together, and says no solution yet when the best match is a problem with no solution to serve it.
purpose: Help each run see the cards and specification records it concerns in one ranked set, and see when no solution covers its request yet.
approach: Select a run's cards and specification records from one combined search, labelled by kind and by source.
out_of_scope: Drafting the wording of a new solution, which a run does when this search reports that none covers the request.
milestones: 1. A combined labelled case set exists, with requests whose right answer mixes cards and records, requests with no solution yet, and requests that match only an ideal or a metric. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The merged pipeline scores at or above the recorded spec_selection balanced score and context_selection pass rate on their own cases, and ahead of the two separate pipelines on the mixed cases.
knowledge: How the two pipelines differ today, stage by stage. Candidates: cards from the card repository; records from the ESOI spec index, rebuilt when a record file changes. Lexical: IDF over a card's name, keywords, summary, terms, symbols and content (adapters/context_store_assembly.py), against field-weighted TF-IDF over the index's own terms (core/spec_selection.py). Vector: the card vector store or the Quest backend's search, against an injected local embedder over record lines (core/repo_specs.py). Fusion: weighted reciprocal-rank fusion with keyword above vector (adapters/hybrid_context_assembler.py), against plain reciprocal-rank fusion. Choice: a balanced-tier filter and a consolidation pass (core/card_filter.py), against a confidence gate that calls a model only for an unclear case. Output: a card result carries no kind, a record result does. Wiring: cards are assembled at the start of every run (core/orchestrator_run_begin.py); records only through tools (core/tools_repo_specs.py) or the deep-goal slice (core/spec_slice.py). A mounted store is read in place and never copied; the same principle holds for records. Context a run needs that is not a solution, read against the evolvable-structure skill: ideals decide what better means ("there are one or more ideals defined for every solution, and a practical metric to compare how well each implementation achieves the relevant ideals"), so a run choosing among alternatives or writing a new solution needs them; metrics are how a change is judged ("alternative implementations are compared via metrics"); an intent's vision statement settles which way to go when a request is ambiguous; problems are the entry point when nothing is built yet ("all solutions are motivated by a defined problem"). Reached by link in the working default: a solution brings its ideals, its metrics and its intent's frame; a problem brings its ideals and its intent. Not reached: a request whose words match only an ideal or a metric, when neither the linked problem nor the linked solution matches it; an intent whose folder holds no problem or solution. Folding the names of a solution's ideals and metric into its searchable text, as a card folds in its keywords, is the planned remedy, unmeasured. Tags (esoi/tags.csv) are a cheap filter or boost for the same search, planned and unmeasured.
measures_of_success: On the mixed cases the expected cards and records are in view under one budget; a request with no solution yet returns its problem or intent with "no solution yet"; on each half neither existing metric drops; an assembly makes one model call or none. Standing conditions: Never copy a record into a card store. Label every result with its kind and its source.
parameters: Candidate pool size per source, fusion weights per source and kind, the gate thresholds, which record kinds are ranked directly and which are reached through links, whether tags filter or boost, the shared character budget, and the assembly deadline.
inputs: The task text and run metadata (scope tags, deadline), the card repository and vector store, and the ESOI spec index of the repository root when one is found.
outputs: One assembled context: ranked items, each with its kind (card, or a record kind), source and id, the linked records each brings, a "no solution yet" mark on a problem or intent that no solution serves, the rendered view under one budget, and the sources for the answer's explanation.
effects: Reads cards and records and writes neither; at most one cheap model call, none for a clear or an empty case.
usage_notes: Built: solutions_and_problems_with_links (core/unified_search.py, with adapters/card_views.py for a card store) answers the read-only tool search_cards_and_specs beside find_specs. A run's context is still assembled by the two pipelines side by side (two_pipelines), and what is selected follows the metric: on 2026-10-22 the merged arm led the mixed cases but held neither half against the best free arm on its own cases (spec_selection, context_selection; numbers in the results log), so two_pipelines stays selected. every_record_a_view stays recorded as the alternative and is not built. A "no solution yet" result is the trigger for the run to define a solution, recorded through track-runs-on-records.

name: Problem-linked tags that identify solutions
description: A flat list of tags that name the risks each solution mitigates, so the solutions a change must consult are found before the change is made.
purpose: Let a person or a run identify, before a change, the solutions that already cover or constrain it, through a short flat list of tags.
approach: Attach to each solution the tags whose linked problems it mitigates, and look up the solutions carrying a tag before a change is made.
out_of_scope: Grouping solutions by topic, and building a hierarchy of tags.
milestones: 1. Every listed tag links the problems it mitigates and passes the mechanical checks (some solution uses it, not every solution does). [met: 2026-10-22] 2. R1 to R4 are each mitigated by at least one tag. 3. Once search-cards-and-specs exists, every tag lowers the share of labelled requests where the right solution is missed.
knowledge: The evolvable-structure skill, Solution, Tags (the owner's words): "Tags: What classifications may be necessary to avoid risk? Possible risks (structural problems): R1: Adding a new solution that duplicates an existing one. R2: Not leveraging the benefits of an existing solution, such as partial overlap of purpose. R3: Not being aware of solutions that need to change definition or implementation due to something else changing. R4: Using a solution when it should not be for the particular use case. Risk Addressed: Every tag should name what risk it mitigates, which are linked problems, whether from the same intent as the solution or from other intents (such as R1-R4 above which are problems defined for ESOI). Consequently, a solution's connected problems are also tags but are not sufficient on their own." R1 to R4 are recorded here as problem records under prob-solution-not-identified until the evolvable-structure library defines them and lets another project's records link a problem. The first list was derived from the risks the problems and the solutions' scoped purposes already name; card-format was added for R3. The specification owner proposed tags in place of area.
measures_of_success: The right solutions are identified before a change; every tag links the problems it mitigates. Standing conditions: Keep the list flat. Create a tag only with its back-fill. Never copy a solution's problem ids into its tags column; the lookup reads them as tags. Retire a tag from every solution in the same commit.
parameters: The list itself: tag, meaning (one sentence a solution can be judged against, yes or no), problem_ids (the problems it mitigates, at least one).
inputs: A solution being written or a change being planned, and the list.
outputs: The solution's tags column; for a planned change, the solutions that share its tags, counting each solution's connected problems as tags (python scripts/esoi_tags.py).
effects: Edits esoi/tags.csv and solutions' tags columns. The QAR check rule Q1 (scripts/esoi_tags.py) fails a tag outside the list, a listed tag with no meaning, a tag that links no problem or a problem id that is not a record, and a tag used by no solution or by every solution; a tag on one solution is printed as a note.
usage_notes: The procedure is in docs/spec-selection.md, Solution tags. The AI adds and retires tags itself. A new tag is created only together with its back-fill: pick from the list first; if none fits, propose a tag with its meaning and the problems it mitigates; judge every existing solution against the meaning; commit the new row and every back-filled solution together. Retirement removes the tag from every solution in the same commit.

name: Index scope decision: which folders and card stores a corpus may read
description: Decides, before anything is read, which folders of a corpus may produce or import cards, keeping dated snapshot copies out while real material stays in.
purpose: Keeps a lane's card memory built from real material, not from dated copies of it sitting in a backups folder.
approach: Decides which folders a corpus may read before any card source reads them, and applies that one decision to every source.
out_of_scope: Deciding whether a single file is readable, and privacy fences, which are set by configuration rather than by this judgement.
milestones: 1. With the folder review unavailable, switched off or failing, no card, import or mount comes from a snapshot series, and the nested store and the docs folder stay indexed. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The lone-snapshot case passes without blocking a single legitimate nested store. [met: 2026-10-22] 3. One read-only run over a real backups folder of dated snapshots, with the verdicts and the time recorded, by decision.
knowledge: The 2026 backups incident: daily snapshots each carrying a card store, 155 stores with 760,608 cards under one folder. The header of context_folder_review.py: on one real corpus most indexable files were a vendored tree present twice and generated data, and judging folders shallow first collapsed thousands of directories into about a hundred decisions in a few batched calls. A cached verdict on the root once excluded the whole corpus, so the root is never excludable. A deterministic exclusion re-opened by its own children let a generated tree back in, so deterministic verdicts are final. The risk gate (commit ac61f64) is pinned by tests/test_folder_review.py and documented in docs/context-card-stores.md, The risk gate.
measures_of_success: Every choose_what_to_index case passes for the selected implementation, apart from those marked as known gaps, with no snapshot taken in where it should be kept out, nothing real lost, no index verdict overruled, and review calls that grow with flagged folders, not files. Standing conditions: never exclude the corpus root; a person's verdict in folder_review.json wins; one decision for every card source.
parameters: QAR_FOLDER_REVIEW (on by default; off means no review call, and flagged folders are then kept out); QAR_SKIP_NESTED_REPOS; the risk thresholds (stores, series length, child-structure similarity) and the review's file-count floor, batch size and depths in the two modules.
inputs: A corpus tree (the walk root and its skip list), the lane's card store folder with any cached folder_review.json, the card sources that will ask (file walk, nested and ancestor imports, mounts), and optionally a model provider for the folder review.
outputs: A FolderGate: the set of corpus-relative folders no card source may read, and of those the risk-flagged ones that could not be reviewed, with why; every card source asks it, so its complement is the set of folders and stores allowed to produce or import cards.
effects: Writes folder_review.json in the lane's card store (verdicts, reasons, source, signals), makes batched folder review calls when a provider is given, and logs one warning per run naming any folder kept out unreviewed and the override.
usage_notes: Call folder_gate once per pass and hand the same gate to every card source; never let a new card source walk or import without asking it. To include a folder the gate turned away, set index true for it in folder_review.json (pinned to keep it against the deterministic safeguards). context migrate-imports shows what the gate turned away without writing anything.

name: Mind: one goal-focused working stream per request
description: Gives every step of a request the same running account of it (what the person asked, what it was resolved to mean, what was refused or corrected, what earlier steps found), carried from step to step instead of rebuilt, so a fast-tier model acts with a continuity one prompt per step cannot give it.
purpose: Keeps every step of a person's request acting on everything the request has established so far, at the cost of the fast tier.
approach: Carries one working stream per request from its first step to its answer, adds only what the admission gate lets in, and reuses the cached part instead of re-sending it.
out_of_scope: What carries across requests and sessions, and deciding which items are worth adding: the stream holds what it is given.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of multi-step requests exists in which a later step needs something established earlier (a refusal, a correction, the resolved request, an earlier finding), and rebuilt_per_step has a recorded result on it. 2. A carried stream scores at or above rebuilt_per_step on that set with the chat judge pass rate held and input cost per request no higher than rebuilt_full_context.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's design: a stream of consciousness focused only on the goal condition of this request, seeing only what relates to it, on the fast tier, because a coding agent is reliable through one long cached session. Read in the code on 2026-10-28, not yet reproduced on a live turn: each planner step is one fresh call (core/orchestrator_planning.py); a cached prefix of head and context layers spans the calls of a turn (core/prompt_layers.py); from the second step the transcript and the context block are swapped for a note saying they were given at step one (core/orchestrator_events.py, on by default in core/orchestrator_constants.py), and that block is where the resolved request, declined proposals, guidance, recent context and cards are prepended (core/orchestrator_run_begin.py); older observations collapse to one line past a recency window (core/planner_context.py). Swapping the context layer also changes the cached prefix, so later steps give up a cheap cache read of the context rather than a full-price one. The final answer still gets the full context. Deep work already runs as one continued session through the deep runner, so this solution concerns the in-process planning loop. From a founder's team meeting on 2026-10-27: the chat is weaker than a task sent to a coding agent because the library is a partial harness; the owner named three directions (near-perfect routing so hard requests reach a deep run, stored context so simple ones need none, or adopting an open-source harness, which the owner placed in the world, as an option to replace the coding agent for doing things: act-in-the-world), and wants high quality from a low-tier model through the structure of prompts and code, with the high tier kept for what matters most, such as plan generation.
measures_of_success: On multi-step requests no later step contradicts, re-proposes or ignores what an earlier step or the person established; the chat judge pass rate holds; input cost per request stays within that of re-sending the context from cache. Standing conditions: Never tell a model it saw something it was not given. Keep the stream inside the request's scope.
parameters: The implementation, the model tier, the stream's token budget and compaction point, and whether the context layer is re-sent, referenced or carried.
inputs: The person's message, the transcript, the resolved request and goal condition, the admitted context and each step's admitted observations.
outputs: Each step's view of the request (a carried message list or a rebuilt prompt), with the step's decision added to it.
effects: Planner-tier model calls; a provider prompt cache is written and read. No store writes.
usage_notes: Selected today: rebuilt_per_step. Compare rebuilt_full_context first, since it is one existing configuration flag, then a carried stream. Decision teamdec_a658ad84e023 (hold, no build).

name: Subconscious: the person's own knowledge, admitted to the working stream by the goal
description: Draws on what the person's own material holds (their cards, files, notes, past conversations and recalled context) and decides at every step what of it enters the working stream, by whether it bears on the request's goal condition, with the scope fence applied once at that gate.
purpose: Keeps each request's working stream holding the part of the person's own knowledge its goal needs, so a fast model is neither misled by near misses nor buried in noise.
approach: Judges each candidate from the person's material against the request's goal condition and scope before it enters the working stream, settling clear cases cheaply and asking a small model only on the borderline.
out_of_scope: Finding the candidates (retrieval, card selection and reading keep their own specifications), and knowledge about the world beyond the person's own material.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of steps exists, each with candidate items marked needed, irrelevant, near miss or out of scope, and recency_window has a recorded result on it. 2. A goal-conditioned implementation admits more needed items than recency_window at the same or better precision, with no out-of-scope item admitted.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's design: the subconscious is the person's own knowledge and context; it does context assembly and tool calls and checks which context is worth showing to the mind. Assembly and reading are already specified (select-context, gather-evidence, search-cards-and-specs, recall-recent-context); this solution adds only the admission check, which no existing record owns. Today cards are filtered once at the start (core/card_filter.py) and observations are admitted by recency (core/planner_context.py). Its value grows with a carried stream, where an admitted item stays for every later step. On cheap-model routing a reviewer handed a decision argued with correct decisions while the same model asked one question of fact did well, so the borderline judge asks whether an item bears on the goal, never whether the plan is right. The specification owner's direction (2026-10-28): intuition is conceptually part of the subconscious. Recorded as outcome_precedents: at admission, past requests like this one and how they ended are surfaced to the working stream as a hint, never as a decision; the outcome history is kept by the long view (hold-the-long-view). The anticipation engine predicts the next ask and recipes replay past successes; neither learns from how a turn ended, so this is new.
measures_of_success: Needed items are admitted, irrelevant and near-miss items are kept out, and no out-of-scope item is ever admitted, at no more than one small model call per step. Standing conditions: Apply the scope fence at the gate on every path. Treat an empty or near-miss lookup as not found.

description: Answers what a request needs to know about the world beyond the person's own material from evidence sources (a host's research and experience search interfaces first, the web after), and says for each claim where it came from and how strong its evidence is.
purpose: Gives people advice and facts about the world they can weigh, from the best evidence the host can reach.

out_of_scope: The person's own material, acting in the world, and deciding which question to research next on the person's behalf.

The specification owner's design: a solution for science that represents world knowledge, using existing interfaces for research and experience search, related to web search. Web research is already specified (search-the-web) and stays the open-web reader this solution calls; the library has no research-source adapter yet, so a host's research or experience search reaches a run today only as a retrieval source or a custom tool. effects: Calls to research sources and the web within a spending cap; no writes.

name: World: doing things outside the host through the best harness, with declared reach and receipts
description: Does the AI's work outside the host's own data (in a workspace, on external tool servers, on other machines, with people on other channels) through the agent harness that scores best on a combined metric, the coding agent today or an open-source harness, answers every capability question from one declared inventory, and returns every outside act with a receipt of what actually ran.
purpose: Gets real work done in the world for people, at the best balance of results, cost and safety, and lets them trust what the AI says it can do and did.
approach: Carries out outside work through the harness configuration the combined metric ranks best, grounds every claim of reach in a declared inventory, and backs every claim of an outside act with a receipt.
out_of_scope: The goal loop, liveness review and outcome reporting around a deep run, which keep their own specifications; knowledge about the world; and changes to the host's own data.
milestones: 1. A small labelled set exists of outside goals, capability questions, out-of-reach requests, setting-blocked claims and claimed acts, and coding_agent_prompt_reach has a recorded combined score on it. 2. Several open-source agent harnesses have recorded combined scores on the same set, and the best of them is the best_open_source_harness arm. 3. The configuration with the best combined score is selected, whether it keeps the coding agent or replaces it.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner corrected an earlier view that the world was only a role tag over existing solutions: it needs its own specification. What exists: a host-supplied reach summary and a stronger-tier reach judge before planning (core/reach_judge.py, off by default), which on cheap-model routing helped most because it asks a fact rather than reviewing a decision; the tool catalog's when-to-use text; the answer check that flags claims of unexecuted work. Open for the owner: whether conversations with other people inside the host belong to the world. Recorded here as yes, because another person's words carry their own consent and scope and lie outside this request's own data; the other reading (the host's own chat is the body's) changes only which solution owns them. The specification owner's direction (2026-10-28): an option to replace the coding agent for doing things in the world with the best open-source harness chosen by a metric, compared with the coding agent, where the metric combines several things. Each implementation is therefore a whole configuration (a harness and a way of declaring reach), ranked by one combined metric.
measures_of_success: Outside goals are met to their done-standard at a cost and time no worse than the coding agent's; capability answers match the inventory; a blocker is stated only after the setting that causes it was read; every claimed outside act has a receipt. Standing conditions: Never describe a capability the inventory does not hold. Never write outside the boundary or read across scope, whatever the harness.
parameters: The harness, the inventory source, which effectors are wired, whether the reach judge runs and on which tier, and the weights of the combined metric.
inputs: The request, the host's inventory of environments and tools with what each allows, and each effector's result.
outputs: A reach verdict for the request (inside, outside, in the world now, or not reachable, with why), and receipts for outside acts (what ran, where, its id).
effects: Reads the inventory; at most one small model call for the reach verdict; no outside act of its own.
usage_notes: Selected today: coding_agent_prompt_reach. The proposal is best_open_source_harness, compared with the coding agent on the same cases; deep runs keep their goal loop and reporting (run-deep-work) whichever harness runs them.

It also knows what the app can do and how it is used, from the host's operations and documentation.
purpose: Lets a person trust what the AI says about their own account and about what it changed in it.
approach: Reads the person's state from the host through one view, changes it only through the host's operations, and re-reads what a change touched before anything is said about it.

knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm.
