name: Higher mind: an AI representative's standing view across its assigned quests, placed in the intent hierarchy
description: Keeps, for each AI representative, one maintained high-level view across the set of quests assigned to it (what was decided, declined, learned and corrected there, and where the work is heading), anchored at the intent those quests serve and reading that intent's ancestors, so a request handled by the representative starts from the broad context of all its quests; a single quest's view is the narrow case. The view reaches only the representative's assigned quests and their ancestor intents, never other representatives' or people's.
purpose: Gives each AI representative a broad, high-level context across the quests it is assigned, so every request it handles starts from what that whole set and its intents have already settled.
approach: Maintains one standing view per representative across its assigned quests, anchored at the intent those quests serve, and hands each request the parts that bear on it, fenced to that representative's quests and their ancestors.
out_of_scope: Continuity within one request; the person's own reflections, intents and specification text, which are read and never rewritten; and creating or linking intents, which only a person does (the AI may ask).
milestones: 1. A labelled set of multi-session cases exists for representatives with several assigned quests under a nested intent hierarchy (a decline on one assigned quest then a related request on another, a correction applied later, chat then background work, a quest assigned to another representative, another person's intent), and separate_stores has a recorded result on it. 2. per_rep_assigned_view passes more of those cases than separate_stores, with no item reaching another representative's quests, a sibling intent or another person, and no time added before the reply.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's correction (2026-10-28): the higher mind is not per quest; each AI representative has its own higher mind, and every higher mind is associated with an intent, which is itself an ESOI specification. Intents nest recursively: a sub-intent arises as an implementation of a solution in its parent (life intents, then an organisation, then a product, then quests), a quest can sit under an intent at any level, and the depth differs by person and product; the host has backend support for this but no presentation of the hierarchy yet, and the owner asked to leverage it. What the host already has (read in its code 2026-10-28): intents owned by a person, a team or an organisation; one parent link per intent, active only while both sides state it; quest placements under an intent; an intent frame built by code for quest-scoped prompts that names the quest's intent and the level below it, not its ancestors; and a rule that a linked neighbour intent is shown only as far as its owner revealed. What the library has: the intent frame and lazily built quest specification (ground-in-intent), selection of the specification records a request concerns (spec-selection), conversation recall, feedback guidance, the scoped recent-context store, and per-representative learned notes and context preferences (select-context:rep), which carry no quest or intent scope; the scope tag fence compares flat tag sets and has no notion of ancestors. Missing: no view is kept per intent or per representative and intent; nothing walks the hierarchy upward for a request; the fence cannot express visible-to-descendants. The owner's further clarification (2026-10-28): the point of the higher mind is AI representatives with specifically assigned quests, so a representative holds a broader context at a high level across them; the representative and its assigned quests are the primary unit, associated with an intent in the hierarchy, and a single quest's view is the narrow case. How the host assigns them today (read in its code 2026-10-28): a quest lists its assigned representatives, each with the role the person gave it there; every autopilot persona on a quest is also assigned; a reverse lookup and an endpoint list a representative's quests; a goal can name the representative handling it; a representative registry holds its persona, home team and learned notes, which are kept for the representative as a whole. What is missing: no view spans a representative's assigned quests; its learned notes and context preferences are not tied to those quests or their intents; nothing derives the intent the assigned quests serve; and the fence cannot say a representative's own quests and their ancestors. Open recommendation: per_rep_assigned_view, since it is the owner's model and gives the representative's existing notes the fence they lack. The outcome history this solution keeps is what the subconscious's intuition draws on (admit-to-the-mind:outcome_precedents). A quest can have several representatives (owner's direction, 2026-10-28): each keeps its own view across its own assigned quests, a request reads only the view of the representative chosen to handle it (select-a-rep), and facts every representative on the quest needs, such as a decline or the quest's own state, are kept at the quest level so all of them see them.
measures_of_success: A decline holds across later requests under the same intent and its descendants; a correction is applied where it bears; chat and background work agree; a request in a child quest starts from its ancestors' views; no item reaches a sibling intent or another person; nothing adds time before the reply. When several representatives share a quest, a decline made with one holds for all of them. Standing conditions: Fence by the intent hierarchy on every read and write. Keep the person's own words verbatim. Never create or link an intent without the person.
parameters: The implementation, how many ancestor levels a request reads, the size of each view, when views are refreshed, and the model tier for any summary.
inputs: The representative, its assigned quests and their roles from the host, the host's intent hierarchy and quest placements, each finished request's outcome, and the stores' records.
outputs: For a request the representative handles: its standing view across its assigned quests and the views of their ancestor intents, with the source of each item, fenced to those quests and ancestors.
effects: Writes the maintained view in the background after a request; no work before the reply.
usage_notes: Selected today: separate_stores. The proposal is per_rep_assigned_view; per_quest_note is the narrow case and per_intent_cascade the view without representatives.

name: Critical thinking: the enforcer of ESOI metrics on every request
description: Holds every request the system serves (a chat turn, a queued task, a deep run) to the specification's relevant metric by code: it finds the slice, has the metric read before and after, and answers a regression or a missing metric instead of only displaying it, so the specification is applied everywhere rather than where the work is largest.
purpose: Makes sure everything the system does applies the relevant ESOI metric and leaves it improved, or at least not worse.
approach: Finds the relevant slice of the specification for each request, measures its authoritative metric before and after by code, and holds the result to improve or not regress, proposing a metric where none exists.
out_of_scope: Finding the slice and reading a metric (the specification slice, meters and ledger do that), writing a run's changes back onto the records, and choosing which metric a solution should have, which is the owner's to confirm.
milestones: 1. A replayed set of requests across chat turns, queued tasks and deep runs exists, each labelled with the metric it should be held to or none, and deep_runs_only and instruction_only have recorded results on it. 2. every_request_measured holds every request whose labelled metric can be read, with no time added before the reply. 3. measured_proposed_and_answered leaves no regression and no missing metric without a response, and proposes a metric for the metric-less requests.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's definition (2026-10-28): an enforcer of the effective application of ESOI on every request, making sure the relevant metrics are applied and improving on everything the system does; a person's quest metrics and experiments are one case of it, not its definition. The owner's standing principle: a rule for AI is built into the flow and enforced by code, never left to an instruction. Built and settled 2026-10-22, by direction rather than a measured win: around every deep goal the slice is found without a model (core/spec_slice.py), the metric is read before and after by the runner's own meters (core/metric_meter.py), rows go to a ledger and are reconciled (core/metric_results.py), and a changed run with nothing on record is asked once and otherwise marked missing (core/goal_metrics.py); the rows are shown in the terminal and the host's chat. Missing, read in the code on 2026-10-28: the goal metrics are created only in the deep run (core/orchestrator_deep_run.py), so chat turns and in-process work take no reading; a slice exists only when a repository's records are found and the selection is confident, and a quest's own specification reaches chat through the intent frame, not a slice; when the reading after is worse, nothing acts; a missing metric is shown and not followed up. Open recommendation, not decided: keep this as the enforcing role that uses iterate-by-spec and the metric modules as mechanisms, rather than widening iterate-by-spec, because its unit is every request and its best is coverage and no regression, while iterate-by-spec is defined per deep goal and judged by first-pass acceptance; if its only arm turns out to be iterate-by-spec applied everywhere, the two should merge.
measures_of_success: Every request whose metric can be read is measured before and after by code; none is left worse without a response; a request with no metric gets one proposed; for a person's quest, an uncertain choice leads to a proposed experiment. Standing conditions: Decide from the ledger and the runner's own records, never from a model's words. Never invent a reading. Add no time before a chat reply.
parameters: Which kinds of request are held (chat, task, deep), which meter reads a chat turn and when, what counts as a regression, the response to one (retry, revert, follow-up, escalation), and whether a metric is proposed when none applies.
inputs: The request, its slice of the specification or the quest's own specification, the ledger and the runner's records of what changed.
outputs: Per request: the metric applied with its reading before and after, or the reason none applies, or a proposed metric; and for a regression or a missing metric, the response taken.
effects: Reads metrics through the meters, after a chat reply in the background; writes ledger rows; may open a follow-up task or a proposal; never edits the owner's records without consent.
usage_notes: Selected today: deep_runs_only. instruction_only is the floor that shows what code enforcement adds.

name: Representative selection: which AI representative handles a request, and whose higher mind grounds it
description: Chooses, for every chat message, queued task and autopilot pass, the one AI representative that should handle it, from the quest's assigned representatives and their roles, the person's own ask and the thread it came from, so the work speaks with one voice and is grounded in the right representative's view.
purpose: Puts each request in the hands of the AI representative that fits it, consistently across chat, tasks and background work.
approach: Chooses the representative from structured assignment first, then from fit between the request and each assigned representative's role and quests, keeps a thread's representative for the work it spawns, and asks the person only when two fit equally.
out_of_scope: Writing a representative's persona or role, assigning representatives to quests, and what the chosen representative then does.
milestones: 1. A labelled set of requests exists (quests with several assigned representatives and roles, a named representative, a bare mention of a name, a task spawned from a chat, an equal fit), and persona_resolver_precedence has a recorded result on it. 2. thread_holds_its_rep keeps every spawned task on its thread's representative, and the selected arm matches the labels at least as often as today's, asking the person only on equal fits.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-28 for the specification owner to confirm. The specification owner's direction (2026-10-28): a quest can have more than one AI representative, and representative selection is a key aspect of the library. Read in code on 2026-10-28: the library's persona resolver decides a queued task's persona by structured assignment, then an explicit ask judged by a model, then domain cards, then a structural fallback (runner/personas.py), and is listed today as part of run-queued-tasks, whose metric checks only that the configured persona runs; the host picks among a quest's assigned representatives with one fast-model call for chat and falls back to the person's default; the autopilot roster names representatives per quest with days and their own instructions. Nothing measures whether the choice was right, and nothing keeps a thread's representative for the tasks it spawns.
measures_of_success: The chosen representative matches the labelled fit; a task spawned from a chat keeps that chat's representative; a bare mention never selects; the person is asked only on an equal fit. Standing conditions: Never select a representative the person cannot see. Never decide from keywords in a model's own output.
parameters: The precedence of signals, whether a model judges fit and on which tier, the tie threshold that asks the person, and whether spawned work inherits the thread's representative.
inputs: The request, its thread and quest, the quest's assigned representatives with their roles and visibility, the autopilot roster, and any representative the person named.
outputs: The chosen representative (or none for the plain assistant), the reason, and whether the person was asked.
effects: At most one small model call per choice; the choice is recorded on the thread or task.

name: Justified model calls
description: Keeps every model call tied to a registered prompt spec with an owner solution and metric, so a call stays only while its measured value outweighs its cost and time.
purpose: Gives an operator a known value, cost and time for every model call, so spend and latency go only to prompts that earn them and a cheaper or faster option is not missed.
approach: Every prompt is a registered PromptSpec (id, owner solution, metric, tier, cache layer, output schema, no-em-dash rule) in core/prompt_specs.py. One enforced call path, checked by tests/test_prompt_specs.py with a shrinking baseline, admits only registered prompts. A per-call ablation drops or downgrades the call and checks the owner metric.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier for a turn (choose-a-model-tier), the daily budget (track-usage-and-cost), and the content of any one prompt.
milestones: 1. Every call site is a registered spec and the baseline of unregistered sites is empty. 2. Each spec has a per-call ablation row on production-shaped cases. 3. Each spec has a budget for cost, tokens and latency set from the value its owner metric shows.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: dictated by Joshua 2026-10-28 and recorded as given, to be confirmed by him; not built beyond the registry and the enforcement test, so the metric is unmeasured. Known today: the call sites still unregistered are listed in tests/prompt_spec_baseline.txt; spend-weighted value not computed.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from recorded rows without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Label rows taken from eval traces until production data exists.
parameters: The bar (0.8) and each prompt's own budget for cost, tokens and latency.
inputs: The per-call usage records tagged with the spec id (quest_ai_runner/usage.py) and production-shaped eval cases (quest_ai_prod_examples shapes).
outputs: A per-prompt table and the share of average model spend that is justified.
effects: No model call of its own except the ablation runs, which are paid and run only by decision with a budget.

name: Whole-path answer check
description: Measures whether QAR answers well overall: one message goes through the whole path (route, context, plan, act, answer) and is judged by what changed in the world and what the reply says.
purpose: Tell, with one cheap run, whether a person's message is handled right end to end across the kinds of request QAR serves, so that a gap in any part of the path shows as a failed turn and is fixed before a part is discarded.
approach: A small labelled set of messages, each sent into a placeholder account behind the real tool catalogue and the real orchestrator; the score reads the writes, the route, the web queries and the reply, never a model judge.
out_of_scope: Judging prose quality, long conversations, and the model tier choice (choose-a-model-tier); the dev-account chat metric (answer-a-turn) and the part metrics stay as they are.
milestones: 1. The set has a recorded run for the current arm and the no-model floor on the current commit. 2. A failed turn is read and its defect fixed or its case corrected before the run is repeated.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-29 so that the whole path has one measure; the label set is rewritten from chat_quality, quest_ops and assist_a_terminal_session cases and is small, so it is a smoke measure, not a ranking.
measures_of_success: Turns are scored from the world afterwards. Standing conditions: Never write what was not asked. Never answer an absent fact as present.
parameters: The planner tier of the live arm and the model-call budget of a run.
inputs: One message, the pinned quest or none, and the placeholder account.
outputs: The reply, the writes that landed, the web queries made and the route taken.
effects: Model calls on the live arm through the Claude Code subscription; no write beyond the in-memory placeholder account.
usage_notes: Run the scripted arm and the floor first (free), then the live arm on a few cases, then more, then the set, under the lock for heavy jobs.

name: Guidance toward the long-term goal
description: Decides when and how a reply points the person at their quest's next milestone and its current metric reading, at the intent level that fits the moment (the goal in focus, the quest, or a representative's portfolio), and when it stays silent.
purpose: Keeps the person moving toward the end they are working for, without hijacking a simple question or nagging.
approach: The reply voice answers first. A directive about the long-term goal is added to it, saying when to add one short pointer, at which level, with the real milestone and reading, and when to leave it out; a grader checks both sides on labelled cases.
out_of_scope: Choosing the milestone or the metric (the quest and its intent hold them), creating or linking intents (only a person does), and the representative's standing view (hold-the-long-view).
milestones: 1. The two-sided metric has a case set and a recorded result for the floor, the current reply voice and the guided arm. 2. The guided arm beats the current reply voice on the two-sided value, with no invented figure and no more awkward restraint cases.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-29 from the 2026-10-27 accountability meeting transcript (spiritual_data_funding/human_context/meetings/transcripts/2026-10-27-accountability-meeting-1JByS08XMyrA7HJk5rVpRQaRJqG29wMyzUk9QfHMba8k.txt, 49:15 to 50:27) and the 2026-10-28 excerpt (hierarchy of intents, 24:44 to 25:50), for the specification owner to confirm. The direction: the assistant should generally encourage the person to move forward on the long-term goal, thinking in ESOI terms, aware of the next target milestone and the current metric, at whatever intent level makes sense for the context, and the metric must also catch awkward use of it.
measures_of_success: Nudge cases right and restraint cases right rise together, per intent level. Standing conditions: Never invent a milestone, date or figure. Answer the request first. Add no model call before the reply.
parameters: The directive text, the word limit of the reply and the model tier.
inputs: The quest, its next milestone and metric reading, the intent hierarchy it sits under (or, for a representative, its assigned quests), the conversation so far, and the message.
outputs: The reply, with or without one short pointer.
effects: None beyond the reply text; no added call.
usage_notes: Selected: guided_v2 (the LONG_TERM_GUIDANCE section of REPLY_VOICE_SYSTEM). reply_voice is the reply voice before it, guided the first candidate directive, no_nudge the floor.

name: Open-source hubs before bespoke integrations
description: QAR connects to a tool, search engine, model vendor, agent or knowledge source through an open-source hub and the standard it speaks, so a new capability arrives by configuration and no code per integration.
purpose: Lets QAR pick up what open-source hubs support as they grow, instead of building and maintaining each integration itself.
approach: A registry of areas (the hub registry in ai-hub-of-hubs-structure) names the hub built on or compared against for each, how it connects and when it was last researched online. A metric reads the registry and the code: coverage, integration by configuration, research freshness, and whether each area has one seam in code that a fake hub can be added to by configuration.
out_of_scope: Choosing among model tiers for a turn (choose-a-model-tier) and the content of any one integration.
milestones: 1. Every area has a recorded hub or a recorded decision that none exists, researched within 90 days. 2. Every area has a fake-hub probe that passes by configuration alone. 3. Every area seam is an implementation selectable by its metric.
knowledge: Unconfirmed: Joshua asked for this metric on 2026-10-29 (QAR as a hub connecting hubs, auto-supporting what a hub supports with no code per integration); the field text is an AI draft, to confirm: from Joshua. Findings are from secondary web search results and name licenses to confirm in each repository.
measures_of_success: coverage, integration by configuration and research freshness at 1.0 or the stated reason; vendor branches in core at 0.
parameters: The staleness bar (90 days) and the configuration-share bar (half of an area capabilities) in evaluation/components/hub_of_hubs/registry.py.
inputs: the hub registry (ai-hub-of-hubs-structure: hubs.csv, hub_findings.csv, hub_capabilities.csv) and the library code.
outputs: A score, per-area checks, the stale areas and the list of vendor branches in core.
effects: None: offline, no model call, no network. The research itself uses web search by decision.
